newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Royal Bank H1 profit not to excite.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Royal Bank H1 profit not to excite.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland, which reports its first half results next Wednesday, is unlikely to excite the market too much, analysts say, but will likely put in a solid performance, its Direct Line insurance unit excepted.
In the half-year to March 31, Royal Bank is expected to post pre-tax profits in a range between 345 and 383 million stg compared to 301 million stg in the comparable period last time.
The figures include an exceptional profit of around 25 million stg from the sale of its U.S. mortgage origination business by Citizens Financial, its 76.5 percent owned U.S. retail banking unit.
A dividend pay-out of 6.2p per share is expected, given the bank's policy of paying an interim dividend equal to a third of its total for the previous year which amounted to 18.6p.
Analysts are still expecting a small profit from Direct Line which has been adversely affected by a sharp price war in its insurance business and an increase in personal injury pay-outs.

Either way, the Direct Line numbers will not make a huge difference to the group result and analysts will be more interested in hearing about how plans to extend Direct Line's business are going as they feel it can do a lot more with what is a good brand name.
"I expect profits at Direct Line to flat at best, said Ian Poulter, analyst at Williams de Broe, "but their corporate lending is doing OK."
Analysts expect the bank's core retail and corporate banking segments to have performed quite well but not spectacularly.
"Royal Bank is doing well in most of its business," said Nick Collier, banking analyst at Morgan Stanley. "They are beginning to see the benefits of restructuring."
Collier expects pre-tax profits in the middle of the range at 369 million stg in the first half.
Analysts are concerned that Royal Bank's profitability, as measured by return on risk-weighted assets, lags behind the rest of the sector, dragged down by Citizens and Direct Line.
The bank has gone for growth to close the profitability gap with credit cards and moves in its corporate banking segment.

As a result of its push into credit cards, bad debt provisions are expected to rise in the first half, also boosted by a rise at Citizens which has already reported net income of $48.3 million for the first quarter compared to $24.8 million last time.
Analysts vary on whether the benefits of Royal bank's cost-cutting exercise Project Columbus have been worthwhile.
"We've been waiting for a long time to see the benefits," said one who declined to be named. "And it hasn't come through sufficiently."
